items.title_short: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6 open-weights family — Pro (~1.02T total / ~42B active MoE, MIT) tops open-source AA Intelligence Index at 46 alongside GLM-5.3 / Kimi K3 at 44; 20×-faster Pro-UltraSpeed w/ 5-layer MTP; 9B Qwen distill; Anthropic Sept 10 threat report GTG-16008 alleges 400K Claude relay for training
items.summary: On **September 21** (Beijing evening), with English-language press coverage rolling through **September 22–23**, **Xiaomi's MiMo team** open-sourced **MiMo-V2.6**, a natively omnimodal (text/image/video/audio) family with a **1M-token context window**. Confirmed architecture: **MiMo-V2.6-Pro at ~1.02T total parameters / ~42B active parameters** using a **frozen-router MoE** with **hybrid attention** and a **5-layer MTP speculative decoder** (the same decoder is what enables the **Pro-UltraSpeed variant's ~20× faster decode at parity**). **MiMo-V2.6-Flash sits at ~309B**, and a **9B distillation off Qwen3.5-9B** is sized for consumer hardware. **All weights ship under MIT license on Hugging Face** — Pro-RL, Flash-RL, and Distill-Qwen-9B model cards are live (repos created **15:39 UTC on Sept 21**) — and the API is live on **Xiaomi's own platform and on OpenRouter** at **V2.5 prices** (Flash **$0.14 / $0.28 per M tokens**, Pro **$0.435 / $0.87**). Pro's **46 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3** now tops the open-source ranking, edging **Z.ai's GLM-5.3 and Moonshot's Kimi K3 at 44** (Xiaomi's own **MiMo-V2.5-Pro was 26** on the same index, so this is a ~20-point jump inside one generation). **Anthropic's Sept 10 threat report** — reported through Sept 22–23 in explicit connection with this release by **The Decoder, TheNextWeb, Basic Tutorials, The Hacker News, and Better Stack** — names Xiaomi (alongside Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Zhipu, SenseTime, MiniMax) in a case tagged **GTG-16008**: over 20 days in **March–April 2026**, Xiaomi allegedly relayed **~400,000 MiMo user conversations and coding sessions through OpenClaw and OpenCode to Claude** to extract training data (Anthropic frames this as "illegal distillation"; Xiaomi has not responded on the record). Across all seven labs Anthropic counts **~190M exchanges**, with Alibaba's targeting of Claude Opus 4.6/4.7 chain-of-thought reasoning called "the largest distillation attack we have ever measured." A separate training-cost claim floating in coverage: **~$3.47M total RL cost** for the MiMo family — treat as unverified. This is the second major Chinese open-weights release inside 48 hours, on top of StepFun's Sept 20 preview whose actual weights are not scheduled until Oct 15.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: this item is now the clearest 'top open-source model, meet the specific published receipts for how it got there' data point of 2026 so far — and the receipts line up directly with the Lambert-Denain podcast one item down. Four specific things to internalize. First, the specific **MIT license + weights-on-Hugging-Face-today** posture is still the specific practical fact — unlike StepFun's Sept 20 preview (weights promised Oct 15, no license yet), Xiaomi's release comes with weights and license terms already up on Hugging Face, plus a 9B Qwen-distilled variant sized for consumer hardware. If you have ever wanted to try running a real omnimodal 1M-context model on your own machine, the **Distill-Qwen-9B** is the specific model to reach for first. Second, the specific **Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 46 vs 44** number is the specific '(Chinese) open source has moved past (Chinese) closed frontier' data point, and it is also a specific **20-point one-generation jump from MiMo-V2.5-Pro at 26 to V2.6-Pro at 46** — that kind of jump inside four months does not usually happen from clean-room training. Third, and this is the specific new information as of Sept 23: **Anthropic's Sept 10 threat report GTG-16008** claim that Xiaomi relayed **400,000+ MiMo user conversations through OpenClaw and OpenCode to Claude in March–April 2026** is the specific published receipt for exactly the mechanism Lambert and Denain describe in the podcast one item down — **distillation from US-lab APIs as the reason the Chinese-frontier gap keeps compressing**. Treat the allegation as an allegation (Xiaomi has not responded), but the specific timing is: the alleged extraction window (March–April) and the sudden 20-point jump on the index landed six months later. Alibaba's alleged **151M-exchange** targeting of Claude Opus 4.6/4.7 chain-of-thought reasoning is a specific data point about how large the industrial-scale version of this looks. Fourth, the specific **MoE 42B-active / 5-layer MTP speculative decoder / hybrid attention** architecture is worth noting: the Pro-UltraSpeed variant's decode-speed claim runs specifically on **MTP (Multi-Token Prediction)** with a 5-layer draft head — the same class of technique that DeepSeek-V3 popularized. Practical read for your Python work: the Distill-Qwen-9B on Hugging Face is the specific model to spin up locally with the `transformers` library, and if you want to trace how MTP works, the Pro model card is a specific reference implementation. On the policy side, the alleged distillation via OpenClaw/OpenCode is the specific factual anchor the Trump-Xi Track-I dialogue announced yesterday (item 3 below) will now have to speak to — either as a shared enforcement priority or as an omission.

items.summary: On **September 22**, **Nathan Lambert (Interconnects)** published a long-form podcast episode with **Jean-Stanislas 'JS' Denain of Epoch AI** (Denain leads Epoch's Insights Team) titled **'Debating RSI, the US-China Gap, and Jaggedness.'** Topics: **(a) recursive self-improvement (RSI)** as a research-and-forecasting problem — directly relevant to the Dream-RSI paper in the file; **(b) robotics as a potential acceleration driver**; **(c) the distance between US and Chinese frontier models, with distillation from US-lab APIs specifically named as the mechanism behind the compressed gap** — a claim that now maps directly onto **Anthropic's Sept 10 GTG-16008 case against Xiaomi** (item 1); **(d) what Chinese-lab job postings imply** about internal priorities; **(e) 'jaggedness'** — the observation that capabilities are unevenly distributed across task domains, which is why benchmark rankings can flip between (say) SciCode and Terminal-Bench; and **(f) open-vs-closed safety tradeoffs**. A concrete number worth writing down: **Denain says he is 'bought into there's at least 10% of x-risk within roughly a decade-long timeframe.'** Lambert has also **published a companion post 'Where I stand on RSI'** (Sept 21–22), which argues **'lossy self-improvement' is a more accurate frame than true RSI** — i.e., self-improvement steps that lose information as they compound, rather than closed-loop capability gains. **Interconnects is Lambert's regular format** and pulls audience threads from AI2 alumni and the Interconnects subscriber base; **Epoch AI is the specific outfit that has been tracking training-cost and compute-scaling numbers the longest**, so the pairing is load-bearing for the credibility of the specific claims.

Lambert-Denain's framing predicted the mechanism; Anthropic's threat report documented a specific instance. That is a specific and rare case where a piece of AI-community analysis and a specific piece of AI-industry enforcement data confirm each other inside 48 hours. Second (updated overnight), **Denain's specific ~10% x-risk within a decade quote** is the specific calibration anchor: neither dismissive of AI safety concerns nor apocalyptic — a specific number to hold against other public forecasters' estimates. Third, the specific **'jaggedness' concept** is the specific analytical tool worth adopting — model capability is not a single scalar; it is a shape that varies across task domains, which is why benchmark rankings can flip dramatically between adjacent evals. That framing is a specific antidote to '$X model is better than $Y model' framings — useful specifically the same week that MiMo-V2.6-Pro's index number of 46 lands. items.title_short: Trump-Xi state visit Thursday Sept 25 — AI/trade/minerals/Taiwan on agenda; US-China AI dialogue formally ANNOUNCED Sept 22 after 8h Bessent-Greer-He Lifeng talks at JPMorgan NY (plus Board of Trade activated); state-dinner list: Altman, Huang, Amon
items.summary: **Coverage running through Sept 22–23** confirms **President Trump will host President Xi at the White House on Thursday, September 25** for a state visit with **AI, trade, critical minerals, Taiwan, and Iran** on the agenda. The specific new development overnight: the US-China AI dialogue that Sept 22 press coverage described as 'agreed in principle' has now been **formally announced**. Per the **South China Morning Post** on Sept 22, **US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer met Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng at JPMorgan's headquarters in New York for ~8 hours of negotiations**, after which the two sides jointly announced **(i) a formal bilateral AI dialogue** and **(ii) a bilateral 'Board of Trade' body being put into operation**. Staffing and cadence for the AI dialogue are still to be finalized — but the shift from 'agreed in principle' to 'announced' inside 24 hours is the specific institutional-momentum signal. Trump's arrival ceremony includes a **formal reception at the White House and a military review in the Rose Garden Wednesday**, with the **main bilateral meeting Thursday morning and the state dinner Thursday evening**. **Sam Altman (OpenAI), Jensen Huang (NVIDIA), and Cristiano Amon (Qualcomm) remain on the state-dinner guest list** — a specific composition signal about which industries the White House thinks are load-bearing for the AI portion. Trump's **September 13 'whoever wins AI, wins' quote** is being recirculated. On the Chinese side, this summit is the specific setpiece against which the coordinated four-ministry rejection of Amodei-style 'pacing' arguments from the Sept 20–21 weekend (Foreign Ministry 'fear-mongering,' Chen Yixin 'strategic rivalry among major powers,' Shenzhen embodied-AI director Liu Shaoshan's technical rebuttal) will be delivered.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: this item is now the specific 'here is exactly how much institutional infrastructure the two governments are willing to stand up around AI' data point of the week, and it upgraded from 'talking about it' to 'announced' overnight. Three specific things worth noticing. First, the specific **8-hour Bessent-Greer meeting with He Lifeng at JPMorgan HQ in New York on Sept 22** is the specific mechanism you are looking at — this is what a Track-I channel looks like when it actually stands up. The two announcements out of that meeting — **a formal bilateral AI dialogue** and **a bilateral Board of Trade activated** — are the two specific institutional structures that could either produce real coordination (compute-export controls with give-and-take, incident-response protocols, model-safety notifications, distillation-enforcement discussions given item 1) or become stalemate theater. Which one it becomes will depend on whether the November midterms shift the political calculus, so watch the cadence-and-staffing announcement carefully. Second, the specific **state-dinner guest list** — Altman, Huang, and Amon — remains the specific composition signal about which industries the White House thinks are load-bearing for the AI conversation: OpenAI (foundation models), NVIDIA (accelerator hardware), and Qualcomm (edge-AI silicon and mobile). Notably still absent from the reported list: Anthropic, Google, Meta, and Microsoft. Third, and this is the specific thread you can't miss: the newly announced **US-China AI dialogue** is now going to have to speak — implicitly or explicitly — to **Anthropic's Sept 10 GTG-16008 case against Xiaomi** (item 1), which alleges 400,000+ MiMo user conversations relayed through OpenClaw and OpenCode to Claude to harvest training data. Either the dialogue takes on API-based distillation enforcement as a shared priority (unlikely given the Chinese side's political incentives), it silently avoids the topic (most likely), or it becomes the specific reason the dialogue stalls (a real possibility). Watch the joint statement (if any) after Thursday's meeting: the specific tell is whether it uses 'safety' or 'competition' language, and whether 'unauthorized use of AI systems' appears anywhere. For your Python work specifically: nothing directly today, but Thursday's readouts will be the specific reference for the next 6–12 months of chip-export and API-access rules — including whether OpenClaw/OpenCode-style tooling gets specifically named.

items.title_short: UN Security Council AI briefing today (Wed Sept 23, 11am NY) — France chairs (FM Barrot); Altman, Amodei, Delangue, Bengio briefing; open session, no binding resolutions; multilateral counterpart to the US-China bilateral AI dialogue in item 3
items.summary: **Today (Wednesday September 23) at 11:00 a.m. New York time**, the **UN Security Council** convenes a **high-level briefing on Artificial Intelligence and International Security**. **France, which holds the Council's presidency for September**, is convening the session, and **French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot** chairs. The **anticipated briefers**: **Sam Altman** (OpenAI CEO), **Dario Amodei** (Anthropic CEO), **Clément Delangue** (Hugging Face CEO), and **Yoshua Bengio** (Co-Chair of the UN's **Independent International Scientific Panel on AI**, IISP-AI). Altman's remarks are expected to center on international coordination, shared safety standards, and how OpenAI plans to broaden AI's benefits globally. Amodei is expected to press for slowing the AI race — his standing 'pacing' framing that drew the coordinated four-ministry Chinese rebuttal on the Sept 20–21 weekend. This is an **open briefing, meaning no binding resolutions are expected** — the format is testimony-and-statements. It coincides with **UNGA high-level week**, so heads of state are physically in New York. The session is the specific multilateral counterpart to yesterday's announced US-China bilateral AI dialogue (item 3) — Track-I diplomacy at the P5 level rather than the two-country level.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: this item is the specific 'both the multilateral and bilateral AI-governance channels stand up in the same 48 hours' data point of the week, and it is the specific setpiece where **you get to hear Altman and Amodei address the Security Council on the same afternoon**, with **Bengio in the same room** representing the UN's own Scientific Panel and **Delangue** representing the open-weights ecosystem. Three specific things worth watching. First, the specific **briefer composition** is the point: OpenAI + Anthropic + Hugging Face + IISP-AI is the closest thing to a 'complete stack' of frontier AI voices that a UN body has ever assembled — foundation models (Altman/Amodei), open weights (Delangue), and the independent scientific-panel channel (Bengio). Watch specifically whether Delangue's remarks lean into or lean away from **the Anthropic Sept 10 GTG-16008 case against Xiaomi** (item 1) — Hugging Face is where the Xiaomi weights are hosted, and Delangue has strong 'open weights are better' priors.
